reason: The liners need support to become growing beds, so fitting them to the metal stock seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect to make supported beds or frames for the liners, though they may still need a growing medium.

alternatives.reason: Breaking up the porous bricks might provide material for the beds, but I want to prepare the liners first.
The nutrient solution seems useful for growing, but the beds are not ready yet.

effect: The liners now have supported shells with separate lower reservoirs, so I can turn to preparing material for the beds.
reaction: The separate reservoirs make me curious about how the beds will be supplied with water.
reason: The porous bricks may make a useful growing medium if broken into smaller pieces.
expectation: I expect the hammer to break the bricks into fragments suitable for further preparation, though I don't yet know whether they can be used directly.

alternatives.reason: Mixing nutrients with drinking water also seems useful, but the troughs may need a growing medium first.
The bricks and metal could form another construction, but their purpose is less clear to me.

effect: The crushed bricks need washing and a leach check before they can go near the roots, so preparing the granules is the next priority.
reaction: The leach check is a useful reminder that a growing medium needs checking before use.
reason: The wash and test bench appears suited to the required cleaning and check.
expectation: I expect the granules to be washed and checked for substances that might leach out, though I don't know whether they will pass immediately.

alternatives.reason: The nutrient solution will likely be useful later, but the growing medium needs preparation first.

effect: The granules passed the leach check and can support roots, but they won't provide nutrients. The next goal also calls for water and air.
reaction: I found the distinction between supporting and feeding roots useful.
reason: Putting the clean granules into the lined troughs seems like the natural next step in preparing the beds.
expectation: I expect the granules to fill the troughs and form a root-supporting medium; the beds may still need water and nutrients.

alternatives.reason: Mixing water and nutrients seems necessary to feed the roots, but I want to assemble the beds first.

effect: The troughs now contain granules that leave air gaps and drain water into the lower reservoirs, helping explain how the beds can give roots both water and air.
reaction: The connection between the granule gaps and drainage is satisfying and useful to understand.
reason: The roots still need water and nutrients, so mixing the concentrate with drinking water seems like the next useful step.
expectation: I expect to make a nutrient solution for the troughs, though it may need a separate step to add it.

alternatives.reason: The bricks and metal can apparently form something, but their purpose is less clear than preparing the nutrient solution.

effect: The nutrient solution is ready to feed the roots, complementing the ceramic granules that support them.
reaction: The distinction between support and nourishment is clear, though the mixing step was predictable.
reason: Adding the solution to the troughs seems like the direct way to supply the beds with water and nutrients.
expectation: I expect the solution to water the beds and reach their reservoirs, though I don't know whether another step will be needed before planting.

alternatives.reason: The bricks and metal may make another useful construction, but its purpose remains unclear.

effect: The solution now circulates through the beds and reservoirs, while drainage leaves air around the roots. Both troughs can be moved separately, and the chapter is complete.
reaction: The explanation of circulation and air gaps brought the separate pieces together satisfyingly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filling the troughs with granules was most worthwhile because it explained how gaps in the medium allow drainage and air around roots.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mixing the nutrient solution was useful but predictable after the explanation that the granules would not feed the roots.

surprise.text: I was interested that the ceramic fragments needed a leach check before use, and that the granules support roots without feeding them.

arbitrary.text: None of my chosen actions felt arbitrary. The offered combination of bricks and metal had an unclear purpose, but I did not try it.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the two beds are used and what the expedition discovers next; the explanations of the growing system made the making feel worthwhile.
